items.title: Bundling GUI libraries via opencv-python

findings.title: opencv-python (bundled Qt) installed into Slicer's Python
findings.explanation: opencv-python ships its own Qt libraries; installing it into Slicer's environment can cause Qt symbol clashes and crashes in Slicer itself and in other extensions. The policy explicitly requires opencv-python-headless instead.
findings.suggestion: Install opencv-python-headless, or avoid OpenCV entirely (the only use seen is cv2.cvtColor/COLOR_GRAY2RGB at line 842).

findings.title: Bundling GUI libraries via opencv-python
findings.explanation: Installing `opencv-python` instead of `opencv-python-headless` bundles GUI libraries (Qt) which conflicts with 3D Slicer's bundled Qt libraries and can cause crashes or windowing issues.
findings.suggestion: Use opencv-python-headless instead of opencv-python.

items.title: Unsafe PyTorch/nnunetv2 installation via pip

findings.title: Unsafe PyTorch/nnunetv2 installation via pip
findings.explanation: Installing `nnunetv2` directly via pip inside Slicer can pull PyPI dependencies including PyTorch, which violates Slicer policy requiring PyTorch to be managed exclusively via PyTorchUtils.
findings.suggestion: Remove direct pip installations of packages that pull PyTorch or manage dependencies through PyTorchUtils.

findings.title: Widget init installs many packages into Slicer's shared environment, including opencv-python and nnunetv2
findings.explanation: nnunetv2 pulls torch from PyPI as a dependency, which violates the policy requirement that PyTorch be installed only through the PyTorch extension. opencv-python (line 371) bundles its own Qt, which the policy flags explicitly; opencv-python-headless is the expected package. Other packages (pandas, blosc2, totalsegmentator, hydra-core, tensorboard) can downgrade or conflict with packages Slicer bundles. The installs are confirmation-gated but still change the shared environment for all Slicer users.
findings.suggestion: Use the NNUNet extension's install logic for nnunetv2 with torch pins handled by PyTorchUtils, use opencv-python-headless, and check each package against Slicer's bundled versions before installing.

items.title: nnunetv2 and totalsegmentator are pip-installed and pull torch from PyPI

findings.title: nnunetv2 and totalsegmentator are pip-installed and pull torch from PyPI
findings.explanation: The module imports nnunetv2 and totalsegmentator and installs them with slicer.util.pip_install when missing. Both packages declare torch as a dependency, so pip resolves torch from PyPI into Slicer's shared environment, bypassing the PyTorch extension/PyTorchUtils that the catalog entry declares as a build dependency. This can replace or shadow the Slicer-managed torch and break other extensions for users who never open this module.
findings.suggestion: Remove nnunetv2/totalsegmentator from the runtime install path, or install them with --no-deps and obtain torch only through PyTorchUtils as the policy requires.

items.title: Blocking input() prompts in a GUI application

findings.title: Blocking input() prompts in a GUI application
findings.evidence: cmd = input("Download sam_vit_b_01ec64.pth from facebook AI? [y]/n: ")
findings.explanation: build_sam.py asks for confirmation on stdin and then calls urllib.request.urlretrieve. Inside Slicer there is no usable stdin, so this either hangs the GUI thread or raises EOFError; the download also has no progress reporting or checksum.
findings.suggestion: Replace with slicer.util.confirmOkCancelDisplay and a background download with progress, or ship the checkpoint via the extension's download mechanism.

items.title: CMake installs only part of the model tree the module reads

findings.title: CMake installs only part of the model tree the module reads
findings.explanation: The resource list covers models/sam/* and models/bone_sam.pth only. The module resolves models/segment_any_muscle, models/ct_segmentation and models/sam2_annotation_tool through resourcePath("UI") + "/../../models/..." (e.g. SegmentHumanBody.py:760-761), and those directories are never installed, so the muscle, CT and SAM2 features fail in an installed build. models/utils.py and models/efficientnet.py are also not installed despite being imported by models/efficientnet.py.
findings.suggestion: Add every directory/file the module imports or opens to MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES (or install the models tree wholesale), and verify from a packaged build.

items.title: Hardcoded developer path in os.system call

findings.title: Hardcoded developer path in os.system call
findings.explanation: The muscle/fat prediction path points at the author's own Windows home directory, so it fails for every other user and on macOS/Linux. It also shells out to whatever 'python' is on PATH rather than Slicer's interpreter, and the return code is ignored so the failure is silent.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the script with self.resourcePath()/moduleDir and run it with slicer.util.launchConsoleProcess or in-process, checking the exit status and reporting errors to the user.

findings.title: Hardcoded developer-machine path in os.system call
findings.explanation: The CT Segmentation path shells out to the system 'python' on a hardcoded path from the author's Windows account. On any other machine the script does not run, and the next line loads a result file that does not exist. On a machine where that path happens to exist, it runs whatever Python is first on PATH outside Slicer's interpreter. This is a broken path and a shell call that bypasses Slicer's environment.
findings.suggestion: Call the script in-process via the module path, use the Slicer Python executable (sys.executable) with an argument list via subprocess, and drop the hardcoded user path.

items.title: Large binaries committed to the repository

findings.title: Large binaries committed to the repository
findings.explanation: bone_sam.pth (46 MB), segment_any_muscle/segmentanymuscle.pth (56 MB) and an 18 MB Miniconda3-latest-MacOSX-arm64.sh installer are committed. This bloats every clone and the extension package, and the Miniconda installer is a redistributable binary that should not ship inside a Slicer extension.
findings.suggestion: Download weights on demand with checksum verification and remove the Miniconda installer from the repository.

findings.title: Large binary model and an installer are committed to the repository
findings.explanation: models/bone_sam.pth (46 MB) is listed as a module resource and committed to git. The tree also contains a 18 MB Miniconda-latest-MacOSX-arm64.sh installer under models/sam2_annotation_tool and a segment_any_muscle .pth of 56 MB. Big binaries inflate every clone and the extension package, and the installer is an unneeded executable. The policy says large binaries should be downloaded on demand. Unverified: I could not read these binaries, so I did not check their contents or hashes.
findings.suggestion: Remove the installer and fetch model weights on demand with checksums, as the module already does for other models.

items.title: Model and code downloads from Google Drive and GitHub at widget init without integrity checks

findings.title: Model and code downloads from Google Drive and GitHub at widget init without integrity checks
findings.explanation: On first open the module clones the repo over the network and downloads several checkpoints (breast VNet, CT nnU-Net, SLM-SAM2) from Google Drive with no hash or signature check. The checkpoints are loaded with torch.load and pickle in-process. A tampered or swapped Drive file would run in the user's Slicer. Each download is behind a confirm dialog, which limits the exposure. Consider pinning revisions and checking SHA-256 for every artifact.
findings.suggestion: Pin the clone to a commit SHA, verify checksums for each downloaded weight, and prefer safetensors or weights_only=True loading.

items.title: Model weights downloaded without integrity verification and loaded with torch.load

findings.title: Model weights downloaded without integrity verification and loaded with torch.load
findings.explanation: Weights are fetched from Google Drive with no checksum or signature check, then deserialized in models/sam/build_sam.py:215 with torch.load(f) without weights_only=True. A substituted or tampered .pth file executes arbitrary Python in the Slicer process with the user's privileges. The same pattern appears in models/utils.py:377 via model_zoo.load_url over plain http.
findings.suggestion: Pin a SHA-256 for each checkpoint and verify after download, and load with torch.load(..., weights_only=True) or map_location plus a safe state-dict loader.

items.title: Multiple packages installed into the shared environment at runtime

findings.title: Multiple packages installed into the shared environment at runtime
findings.explanation: timm, einops, gdown, blosc2, pandas and pywintypes are all imported and pip-installed on demand into Slicer's shared Python. Each install mutates the environment for every extension and can pin or upgrade numpy/scipy/pillow as transitive dependencies. pywintypes is also not a valid PyPI distribution name (pywin32 provides it), so that install path is broken.
findings.suggestion: Bundle what is needed in the extension's own wheel/venv, or document and gate each install behind an explicit confirmation dialog; fix the pywintypes import to pywin32.

items.title: Non-commercial license and missing third-party license texts

findings.title: Non-commercial license and missing third-party license texts
findings.evidence: set(EXTENSION_DESCRIPTION "SegmentHumanBody aims to asist its users in segmenting MRI medical data on 3D Slicer by integrating varios deep learning models developed by Mazurowski Lab. SegmentHumanBody has CC BY-NC 4.0 license which does not allow commercial use.")
findings.explanation: CC BY-NC 4.0 permits redistribution but forbids commercial use, so users and clinical deployments must be told. The bundled Meta SAM/SAM2 sources are Apache-2.0 (headers say 'licensed under the license found in the LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree') but no Apache-2.0 text is included, and the license of the bundled .pth weights and the Miniconda installer is not stated.
findings.suggestion: Add the Apache-2.0 text for the bundled SAM/SAM2 code, state the license of each model checkpoint, and surface the non-commercial restriction in the README and module UI.

items.title: Runtime installation of remote source archive

findings.title: Runtime installation of remote source archive
findings.explanation: Downloading and installing arbitrary code archives from GitHub via pip at runtime without user consent verification or integrity checks poses security and stability risks.
findings.suggestion: Declare external dependencies properly in CMake and packaging rather than installing via zip URL at runtime.

items.title: createFeatures deletes every file in a folder without checking its contents

findings.title: createFeatures deletes every file in a folder without checking its contents
findings.explanation: The code unconditionally removes all files matching * in featuresFolder. If that folder is ever configured to a user directory (or the default resolves outside a temp dir), user data is destroyed without confirmation. I could not verify where featuresFolder is set, so the blast radius is unconfirmed.
findings.suggestion: Use a dedicated temporary directory created with tempfile.mkdtemp(), or restrict deletion to files matching the expected *_features.pkl pattern.

items.title: Global git config changed on widget init

findings.title: Global git config changed on widget init
findings.explanation: The module changes the user's global git configuration, outside the extension's own scope, as a side effect of opening the module.
findings.suggestion: Remove the global git config change, or pass the setting per repository.

items.title: Global sys.path mutation in a model module

findings.title: Global sys.path mutation in a model module
findings.explanation: Importing this module appends a directory to the process-wide sys.path, which can shadow Slicer's own modules for the whole session. It is a side effect at import time rather than a local import.
findings.suggestion: Use relative imports or importlib with an explicit path instead of mutating sys.path.

items.title: Malformed icon URL in module CMakeLists

findings.title: Malformed icon URL in module CMakeLists
findings.explanation: The URL omits the branch segment (/main/), so it resolves to a non-existent path. The root CMakeLists.txt:11 has the correct URL; the duplicate in the module file is wrong.
findings.suggestion: Remove the duplicate EXTENSION_* variables from the module CMakeLists or fix the URL to include /main/.

items.title: Model imports may fail: SAM_LST uses undefined names

findings.title: Model imports may fail: SAM_LST uses undefined names
findings.evidence:
from sam import sam_model_registry
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torchvision.models.resnet import resnet18
findings.explanation: The file imports 'sam' as a top-level module and uses 'os' without importing it, so it cannot load inside the extension. It is not in the CMake list, so it is dead code, but it shows that not all bundled modules were tested. Also, the module-level 'args = cfg.parse_args()' at SegmentHumanBody.py:24 runs argparse on import.
findings.suggestion: Remove unused model files, or fix the imports and add tests.

items.title: Model-specific subprocess call uses a hardcoded Windows path and os.system

findings.title: Model-specific subprocess call uses a hardcoded Windows path and os.system
findings.evidence:
command = (f"TotalSegmentator -i {input_path} -o {output_path} "
                f"--roi_subset vertebrae_T12 vertebrae_L3 vertebrae_L4")
      print(f"Running command: {command}")
      os.system(command)
findings.explanation: The command is built by string interpolation and run through the shell. Paths containing spaces or shell metacharacters break or inject commands. The input path comes from the user's volume filename, so this is a command injection path on the user's own machine. Severity is minor because the user already controls the input.
findings.suggestion: Use subprocess.run with an argument list and no shell.

items.title: No automated tests

findings.title: No automated tests
findings.explanation: The only test registration is commented out. SegmentHumanBody/CMakeLists.txt:52 registers a unittest against SegmentHumanBody.py, but no test class was visible in the module, so there is effectively no coverage of the segmentation or label-assignment logic.
findings.suggestion: Add a real module test with a small sample volume and enable it in Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt.

findings.title: No test coverage; testing is commented out
findings.explanation: The only test registration is commented out, so there is no automated check that the module loads or that the models run. This is non-blocking, but it makes the install-and-download behavior above hard to validate.
findings.suggestion: Add a minimal load test that does not download weights, and a smoke test on sample data.

items.title: No sample data, validation, or clinical-use disclaimer

findings.title: No sample data, validation, or clinical-use disclaimer
findings.evidence:
- Load an image to be segmented.
- Choose **Modules > Segmentation > SegmentHumanBody** module in the module selector. The first time the module is started, it will ask permission to install pytorch. Give permission and wait several minutes for the installation to complete. The application will not be responsive during the installation.
findings.explanation: The README gives a usable workflow and screenshots, but there is no sample dataset, no accuracy/validation information for the bundled models, and no statement that output is not for clinical use. The README also confirms the first-run install blocks the GUI for several minutes.
findings.suggestion: Add a small sample volume, cite validation results for SegmentAnyBone, and add a research-use-only disclaimer.

items.title: Non-commercial license restricts use of extension and weights

findings.title: Non-commercial license restricts use of extension and weights
findings.explanation: CC BY-NC 4.0 permits distribution but prohibits commercial use. The extension description and the module's warningDisplay state this, so users are informed. Bundled third-party model weights (SAM, SegmentAnyMuscle, SLM-SAM2, nnU-Net) may carry their own terms that I did not verify. The grant itself is not missing and does not prohibit distribution.
findings.suggestion: Confirm that the upstream model licenses allow redistribution under CC BY-NC, and list them in the README.

items.title: pickle used for feature caches

findings.title: pickle used for feature caches
findings.explanation: Features are written with pickle.dump (line 846) and read back with pickle.load. The files are self-generated, so risk is low, but any file placed in that folder by another process would be deserialized as arbitrary Python.
findings.suggestion: Use np.save/np.load or torch.save with weights_only=True for the feature cache.

findings.title: pickle.load used on cached feature files
findings.evidence:
with open(self.featuresFolder + "/slice_" + str(currentSliceIndex) + "_features.pkl" , 'rb') as f:
                      self.sam.features = pickle.load(f)
findings.explanation: Feature files are written by the module itself (line 846) into the module resource folder, so exploitation needs write access to that folder. The unpickle is still unsafe in principle if the folder is shared or the files are copied from elsewhere. Note the same pattern at line 1461.
findings.suggestion: Store features as .npy or safetensors and load with allow_pickle=False.
